name: MM Post Grid
author: MM Web

sections.description:
MM Post Grid displays your posts, pages or any custom post type in a responsive card grid. Add one shortcode and you get a grid that already looks finished, with sensible spacing, readable typography and a hover state that does not shout.

It is built to be a good neighbour. The grid inherits your theme typeface instead of forcing its own, every class name is prefixed, no global element is styled, and there is not a single !important in the stylesheet. Nothing is loaded on pages that do not contain a grid.

What makes it different

  • Genuinely lightweight. One small stylesheet and, only when you use Load More, one small script. No jQuery on the front end, no CSS framework, no icon font, no external requests.
  • Loads nothing where there is no grid. Assets are registered up front and enqueued only when a grid actually renders.
  • Theme friendly. Font family is never set, so the grid picks up your theme typeface and only controls size and rhythm. All selectors are scoped to the .mmpg wrapper.
  • Accessible by default. Real heading levels you choose, no duplicate links per card, unique accessible names on every Read more link, visible focus rings, a live region for Load More, and full support for prefers-reduced-motion.
  • Customisable without CSS. Over 35 styling settings drive CSS custom properties: card layout, hover and image effects, spacing, typography, line clamping, category badges, button styles and pagination alignment. Only the values you actually change are printed, so a default site sends no extra CSS at all.
  • Seven styling templates. Default, Minimal, Soft, Outline, Dark, Magazine and List. Apply one as a starting point, then fine-tune anything on the Styling tab.
  • Three card layouts. Image above the text, image beside the text, or text laid over the image. The side-by-side layout only engages when a card is wide enough, so it never gets squeezed.
  • Per grid overrides. Any setting can be overridden on a single grid through a shortcode attribute.
  • Works without JavaScript. The Load More control is a real link to the next page, so it degrades to normal pagination.
  • Developer friendly. Namespaced classes, a documented filter on every piece of markup, and no third party dependencies.

Usage

[mm_post_grid]

That uses your saved settings. Add attributes to override them for one grid:

[mm_post_grid columns="4" posts_per_page="8" pagination="load_more"]

Shortcode Attributes

Every attribute is optional. Anything you leave out falls back to your saved setting.

Query

  • post_type – One or more post types, comma separated. Default: your setting.
  • posts_per_page – Number of posts per page, 1 to 48.
  • orderby – date, modified, title, menu_order, comment_count, rand or ID.
  • order – ASC or DESC.
  • category – Category slugs or IDs, comma separated.
  • categories – Alias of category.
  • tag – Tag slugs or IDs, comma separated.
  • taxonomy – A taxonomy name, used together with terms.
  • terms – Term slugs or IDs for the taxonomy above.
  • author – Author IDs, comma separated.
  • exclude – Post IDs to leave out.
  • offset – Skip this many posts.
  • ignore_sticky – yes (default) treats sticky posts like any other post; no pushes them to the front.

Layout

  • columns – Desktop columns, 1 to 6.
  • columns_tablet – Columns below 1024px, 1 to 6.
  • columns_mobile – Columns below 640px, 1 to 6.
  • gap – Space between cards in pixels, 0 to 80.
  • image_size – Any registered image size.
  • image_ratio – 16-9, 16-10, 3-2, 4-3, 1-1, 3-4 or auto.
  • pagination – none, numbers, prev_next or load_more.

Content

  • show_image – yes or no.
  • show_title – yes or no.
  • show_date – yes or no.
  • show_author – yes or no.
  • show_category – yes or no.
  • show_excerpt – yes or no.
  • show_read_more – yes or no.
  • image_fallback – yes or no, show a placeholder when a post has no featured image.
  • title_tag – h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, p or div. Pick the level that fits the page outline.
  • excerpt_length – Words, 0 for the untrimmed excerpt.
  • read_more_text – Link label.
  • button_style – link, button or outline.

Style

These switch a class on the grid, so one grid can look different from the site-wide styling. Colours and sizes stay site-wide on the Styling tab.

  • card_layout – stacked (image above the text), horizontal (image beside the text once the card is wider than 460px) or overlay (text over the image).
  • hover_effect – lift, shadow, border or none.
  • image_hover – zoom, none or grayscale.
  • text_align – left or center.
  • term_style – text or badge.
  • button_size – small, medium or large.
  • pagination_align – left, center or right.
  • title_lines – Clamp titles to this many lines, 0 to 5. 0 shows the full title.
  • excerpt_lines – Clamp excerpts to this many lines, 0 to 8.

Wrapper

  • class – Extra class names on the wrapper.
  • id – A specific HTML id, useful for anchor links.

Examples

[mm_post_grid columns="4" posts_per_page="12" pagination="numbers"]

[mm_post_grid category="news,events" show_excerpt="no" title_tag="h2"]

[mm_post_grid post_type="portfolio" taxonomy="project_type" terms="print" image_ratio="1-1"]

[mm_post_grid posts_per_page="9" pagination="load_more" button_style="button"]

[mm_post_grid card_layout="overlay" columns="2" image_ratio="4-3" title_lines="2"]

[mm_post_grid card_layout="horizontal" columns="1" term_style="badge"]
sections.installation:
1. Upload the mm-post-grid folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the ZIP through Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen.
  3. Open Post Grid in the admin menu to set your defaults.
  4. Add [mm_post_grid] to any post, page, template or widget area.
sections.faq:
Does it work with my theme?

That is the main design goal. The grid never sets a font family, never styles a global element, and scopes everything to its own wrapper. If your theme does something unusual you can turn the stylesheet off completely on the Advanced tab and write your own.

Does it need a page builder or block editor?

No. It is a shortcode, so it works in the block editor Shortcode block, in the classic editor, in a widget, or in a template through do_shortcode().

What do the styling templates change?

Only the values on the Styling tab. Posts, columns, pagination and card content are never touched. A template is a starting point, not a mode: after applying one you can change any value, and the Templates tab shows the styling as custom from then on.

Why is the pagination not using my card colours?

Pagination and the load more button sit on your page rather than on a card, so they use the button colours and inherit your theme text colour. That way a dark card template never makes them unreadable on a light page.

Is there a Gutenberg block?

Not in 0.1. Rendering is fully separated from the shortcode internally, so a block is planned as a thin addition without changing any output.

Can I show a custom post type?

Yes. Set the default on the settings screen, or pass post_type="portfolio". Several types work too: post_type="post,page".

Can I use more than one grid on the same page?

Yes, including several paginated grids. Each grid gets its own page query variable so they do not move together.

Does Load More work without JavaScript?

The button is a real link to the next page. Without JavaScript, clicking it loads the next page normally.

Will it slow my site down?

The stylesheet is small and only loads where a grid renders. Featured image data is preloaded in one query to avoid a query per card, and the row count query is skipped when pagination is off.

What happens to my settings when I delete the plugin?

Nothing is removed unless you ask for it. Tick the option on the Advanced tab before deleting if you want the settings row gone.
sections.changelog:
0.1

  • Initial release.
  • [mm_post_grid] shortcode with per grid attribute overrides.
  • Tabbed settings screen: General, Content, Templates, Styling and Advanced.
  • Seven styling templates applied with one click, extendable through the mmpg_templates filter.
  • Three card layouts, four hover effects, three image hover effects, category badges, outline buttons, line clamping and pagination alignment.
  • Four pagination modes, including a progressively enhanced Load More.
  • Responsive column control for desktop, tablet and mobile.
  • Styling through CSS custom properties, with an option to disable the stylesheet.
  • Full set of filters and actions for developers.
  • Translation ready, ships with a POT file.
